result.title: How to Get Past the “Messy Middle” of a Big Change | Mary Martin | TED
result.description:
Did progress on your next big project stall out? Transformation expert Mary Martin refers to this moment as the "messy middle" — the frustrating gap between starting and finishing a goal, when you might lose confidence or give up altogether. Offering three ways to find glimmers of progress when the going gets tough, she explores what to do when you feel stuck. (Recorded at TED@BCG on October 23, 2025)

result.title: Burnout shouldn’t be the price of your success #TEDTalks
result.description: Burnout shouldn’t be the price of success, but setting boundaries at work is easier said than done. Tarveen Forrester, who oversees workplace culture at Kickstarter, shares practical strategies for protecting your time and cultivating “sustainable ambition,” so you can crush your goals — without letting them crush you.

result.title: How Citizens (Not Politicians) Are Building the Future | Jon Alexander | TED
result.description:
Citizen strategist Jon Alexander spent a decade gathering stories of democracy in action — and found that most change doesn't come from politicians or institutions. He shares examples from across the globe of ordinary people working together to improve their lives and communities, showing why the key to fixing things may already be in your own hands. (Recorded at TED Democracy Philadelphia on June 13, 2026)

result.title: A Cosmologist’s Guide to the End of the Universe | Katie Mack and Debbie Millman | TED
result.description:
How does studying the end of time change your perspective of life on Earth? Cosmologist and TED Fellow Katie Mack joins designer and podcaster Debbie Millman to talk about the story of the cosmos — from the Big Bang's ancient light still glowing across the universe to the five ways it might all come to an end — plus what aerobatic flying taught her about staying present. (Recorded at TEDNext 2025 on November 10, 2025)

result.title: Just one conversation can make a difference #TEDTalks
result.description: Can you stand up for what you believe in without participating in politics? Anti-career coach Danielle Roberts and political rule breaker Katie Paris discuss how to rethink power, work and civic life on your own terms. They explore how rest, community and meaningful participation can help you stay engaged in the issues shaping your life. (This conversation is part of “Idea Knock Down,” a series where two people with different perspectives take on big questions — one block at a time.)
